patient_has_structural_traumatic_brain_i.assessment: Chart describes impaired movement, asymmetrical pupils, GCS 6, drowsiness, vomiting – all suggest structural brain injury following head trauma, even though CT was deferred.
patient_has_structural_traumatic_brain_i.evidence: Half an hour after the fall the child became drowsy, pale, and vomited... Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) was 6/15, the pupils were asymmetrical and movement of the right upper and lower extremities was impaired.

patient_has_structural_traumatic_brain_i.assessment: Severity qualifies as more than mild; GCS 6/15 is severe. Chart supports structural TBI, but not mild/moderate severity.

patient_has_undergone_computerized_axial.assessment: CT scan was advised but specifically deferred; chart confirms no imaging was performed yet.
patient_has_undergone_computerized_axial.evidence: The neurosurgical team advised deferring the CT scan in favor of initiating immediate treatment.

patient_has_undergone_computerized_axial.assessment: No CT was performed, so no evidence of brain contusion identified radiographically.
No CT was performed, so no evidence of epidural hemorrhage radiographically.
No CT was performed, so no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage radiographically.
No CT was performed, so no evidence of intraparenchymal hemorrhage radiographically.
No CT was performed, so no evidence of skull fracture radiographically.
No CT was performed, so no evidence of subarachnoid hemorrhage radiographically.
No CT was performed, so no evidence of subdural hemorrhage radiographically.

patient_has_finding_of_hospital_patient_.assessment: The patient was transferred to the emergency department following neurological deterioration and is receiving immediate treatment, indicating they are currently admitted to the hospital as an inpatient at the time of screening.
patient_has_finding_of_hospital_patient_.evidence: He was transferred to the emergency department... The neurosurgical team advised deferring the CT scan in favor of initiating immediate treatment.

patient_blood_ethanol_measurement_value_.assessment: The chart contains no mention of blood ethanol (alcohol) measurement or intoxication; as this is not a vignette-typical fact in pediatric trauma, default to null.

__THRESH__::patient_blood_ethanol_measur.assessment: There is no evidence in the chart to suggest significant alcohol ingestion or measurement; in an 8-year-old, such detail would be included if present; default to FALSE.
__THRESH__::patient_blood_ethanol_measur.evidence: silent: pediatric vignette would mention alcohol presence if positive

patient_does_not_have_both_eyes_now.assessment: Pupils were assessed as symmetrical and reactive at the scene, indicating the child has both eyes.
patient_does_not_have_both_eyes_now.evidence: pupils were symmetrical, reactive to the light

patient_does_not_open_eyes_now.assessment: GCS score of 6 implies eye opening is either absent or only to pain, but explicit chart data does not confirm persistent inability to open eyes; default to FALSE.
patient_does_not_open_eyes_now.evidence: GCS 6/15 (but eye opening component not directly stated); silent: defer to visit

patient_has_finding_of_anophthalmos_now.assessment: Pupils were noted as symmetrical and reactive, indicating both eyes are present.
patient_has_finding_of_anophthalmos_now.evidence: pupils were symmetrical, reactive to the light

patient_has_finding_of_burn_now.assessment: There is no mention of burns at the scene, in transport, or upon arrival; as burns would be mentioned in trauma documentation, set to FALSE.
patient_has_finding_of_burn_now.evidence: silent: absence of burn noted in trauma context

patient_has_finding_of_disability_now.assessment: Although the patient is currently neurologically impaired (GCS 6 and right-sided weakness), there is no mention of pre-existing (baseline) disability; this exclusion targets baseline disabilities, so set to FALSE.
patient_has_finding_of_disability_now.evidence: silent: no mention of pre-existing disability

patient_has_finding_of_disability_now@@r.assessment: No baseline disability reported; acute neurological deficits relate to the presenting injury, not to a chronic/previously present state; this exclusion targets baseline disability.
patient_has_finding_of_disability_now@@r.evidence: silent: deficits are acute, not pre-existing

patient_has_finding_of_extensive_injury_.assessment: The patient presented with rapid neurological decline (drowsiness, vomiting, decreased GCS, asymmetric pupils, limb impairment) and vital signs (bradycardia, hypertension) consistent with elevated intracranial pressure and risk of herniation, indicating an extensive injury with clinical instability.
patient_has_finding_of_extensive_injury_.evidence: Upon arrival the heart rate was 52/min, blood pressure of 155/98. The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) was 6/15, the pupils were asymmetrical and movement of the right upper and lower extremities was impaired. The neurosurgical team advised deferring the CT scan in favor of initiating immediate treatment.

patient_has_finding_of_extensive_injury_.assessment: Bradycardia (HR 52/min in an 8-year-old is well below normal) and hypertension (BP 155/98) are abnormal vital signs in a child and suggest acute hemodynamic instability associated with raised intracranial pressure.
patient_has_finding_of_extensive_injury_.evidence: heart rate was 52/min, blood pressure of 155/98

patient_has_finding_of_extensive_injury_.assessment: The patient is medically unstable as evidenced by rapid worsening of neurological status, vomiting, drowsiness, and abnormal vitals, necessitating emergency intervention.
patient_has_finding_of_extensive_injury_.evidence: the child became drowsy, pale, and vomited... Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) was 6/15

patient_has_finding_of_extensive_injury_.assessment: Immediate neurosurgical intervention was warranted as per the team's decision to defer imaging due to critical status, indicating surgical instability.
patient_has_finding_of_extensive_injury_.evidence: The neurosurgical team advised deferring the CT scan in favor of initiating immediate treatment.

patient_has_finding_of_multiple_injuries.assessment: There is no chart evidence of multiple injuries; only head injury and its sequelae are described.
patient_has_finding_of_multiple_injuries.evidence: An 8-year-old boy fell from his bike striking his left temple... movement of the right upper and lower extremities was impaired.

patient_has_finding_of_multiple_injuries.assessment: There is no evidence of multiple injuries causing hemodynamic instability; instability is attributable to the head injury alone.
patient_has_finding_of_multiple_injuries.evidence: Chart describes only a single head injury; all instability findings follow from this.

patient_has_finding_of_multiple_injuries.assessment: There is no evidence of multiple injuries causing medical instability; instability is related solely to the head injury.
There is no evidence of multiple injuries causing surgical instability; all surgical urgency is due to the head injury.
patient_has_finding_of_multiple_injuries.evidence: Only head trauma requiring urgent management is mentioned.

patient_has_finding_of_visual_acuity_no_.assessment: The chart states that at the scene, pupils were reactive to light, and there is no later note of complete loss of light perception.
patient_has_finding_of_visual_acuity_no_.evidence: pupils were symmetrical, reactive to the light

patient_has_obvious_intoxication_now.assessment: There is no mention of intoxication; the clinical context is accidental trauma in a child with no behavioral or laboratory suggestive findings.

patient_has_finding_of_penetrating_wound.assessment: Chart describes a blunt injury to the temple; there is no mention of any penetrating wound.
patient_has_finding_of_penetrating_wound.evidence: An 8-year-old boy fell from his bike striking his left temple on the pavement.

patient_has_finding_of_penetrating_wound.assessment: There is no mention of any penetrating wound, minor or otherwise.
patient_has_finding_of_penetrating_wound.evidence: An 8-year-old boy fell from his bike striking his left temple on the pavement.

patient_has_finding_of_severe_multiple_i.assessment: Chart describes impaired movement on one side, drowsiness, abnormal pupils, and calls for immediate neurosurgical treatment, but only a traumatic brain injury is described; there is no evidence of multiple (i.e., >1 system/region) severe injuries.
patient_has_finding_of_severe_multiple_i.evidence: movement of the right upper and lower extremities was impaired. The neurosurgical team advised deferring the CT scan in favor of initiating immediate treatment.

patient_has_finding_of_severe_multiple_i.assessment: Blood pressure is elevated and heart rate is slow, but there is no explicit mention of hemodynamic instability due to multiple injuries (rather, these findings likely relate to brain injury). Chart does not describe shock or unstable cardiovascular status from multiple injuries.
patient_has_finding_of_severe_multiple_i.evidence: heart rate was 52/min, blood pressure of 155/98

patient_has_finding_of_severe_multiple_i.assessment: The patient is described as drowsy, pale, and vomiting, with low GCS, but instability appears attributable to a single trauma (brain injury), not multiple severe injuries. No evidence of medical instability from multiple injuries.
patient_has_finding_of_severe_multiple_i.evidence: Half an hour after the fall the child became drowsy, pale, and vomited.

patient_has_finding_of_severe_multiple_i.assessment: There is no evidence in the chart of surgical instability from multiple severe injuries; only neurosurgical (single-system) concern is described.
patient_has_finding_of_severe_multiple_i.evidence: The neurosurgical team advised deferring the CT scan in favor of initiating immediate treatment.

patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_injury_.assessment: The child has suffered an acute traumatic brain injury after a fall.
patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_injury_.evidence: An 8-year-old boy fell from his bike striking his left temple on the pavement.

patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_injury_.assessment: The injury caused significant sequelae (drowsiness, vomiting, impaired movement, low GCS), so it is not 'insufficiently traumatizing.'
patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_injury_.evidence: GCS was 6/15, the pupils were asymmetrical and movement of the right upper and lower extremities was impaired.

patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_and_or_.assessment: The patient suffered a fall striking his head and exhibited neurological symptoms, supporting a current traumatic injury.
patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_and_or_.evidence: An 8-year-old boy fell from his bike striking his left temple... pupils were asymmetrical and movement of the right upper and lower extremities was impaired.

patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_and_or_.assessment: There is no evidence of an anoxic injury; the described injury is traumatic from a fall.

The chart describes a traumatic brain injury with a GCS of 6 and focal findings; however, it does not establish mild structural TBI since imaging was deferred and severity appears greater than mild. Applying exclusion default since inclusion-defining entity not confirmed.
patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_and_or_.evidence: GCS was 6/15, pupils were asymmetrical and movement... impaired. CT scan deferred; severity exceeds mild TBI parameters.

patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_and_or_.assessment: No mental/psychiatric injury is described; symptoms are neurologic/physical.
Neurological impairment and reduced GCS (6/15) imply difficulty completing tasks.
patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_and_or_.evidence: GCS was 6/15, pupils were asymmetrical and movement of... extremities was impaired.

patient_is_pregnant_now.assessment: The patient is an 8-year-old boy, cannot be pregnant.
